title: Spectral loop scores gave no clear link to regional projection direction in 22 larval zebrafish
abstract: We tested whether spectral loop scores align with regional projection direction in 22 larval zebrafish. Public calcium records and a cross-animal projectome shared 57 atlas regions. We formed imaginary coherency products for 29,260 dependent triples at each frequency before averaging. The primary mean alignment was 0.0040, with a 95 percent fish interval from -0.0055 to 0.0137 and exact two-sided p=0.4417. Mean segment agreement was 0.0485. Planned processing checks and a post hoc shared-ROI exclusion did not resolve primary alignment. A fixed directed-ring control gave opposite loop signs at two frequencies. A reversible finite-record control gave nonzero estimated loop sizes despite zero population loops. The test therefore gives a limited null result for these scores, not evidence that wiring has no role in dynamics. Short records, slow calcium signals, regional mixing, leakage and a projectome from other animals limit inference. Original code, aggregate evidence, input hashes and separate-data retrieval steps support reproduction. Job sci-1107-hp-neural-structure-and-computation-1bc654e24e0d; machine hp; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: Mean alignment and segment agreement in 22 fish. Small points are fish. Large points and bars show means and nominal 95 percent fish bootstrap intervals. Triangles are dependent and share one projectome.

The same directed ring gives opposite imaginary loop signs at two frequencies. A real population spectrum gives nonzero finite-record estimates. These synthetic controls are not a fitted null for the fish.

Frequency averaging can break cancellation. We form each product before bin averaging, while retaining leakage as a limitation.
